title: Inside of an atom
competency: Describe the structure of an atom and find the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons.

keywords.def: The tiny, dense centre of an atom. It holds the protons and neutrons.
A particle in the nucleus with a relative charge of +1 and a relative mass of about 1.
A particle in the nucleus with no charge and a relative mass of about 1.
A particle outside the nucleus with a relative charge of −1 and almost no mass.
The path (energy level) around the nucleus where electrons are found.
The number of protons in the nucleus, written Z. In a neutral atom it also equals the number of electrons.
The number of protons plus the number of neutrons, written A.

en.text: An atom has a tiny, dense nucleus with protons (+1) and neutrons (0), and electrons (−1) moving in shells around it. Protons and neutrons each have a relative mass of about 1; an electron is about 1800–2000 times lighter. An atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons, so it is neutral.

screens.title: Where is the mass?
screens.ask: Most of the MASS of an atom is in which part?
screens.after: The nucleus. Protons and neutrons are much heavier than electrons. But the electrons take up most of the space!

screens.title: Subatomic particles
paras: An atom consists of a tiny dense nucleus surrounded by electrons.
Atoms are made of even smaller particles called subatomic particles.

screens.title: Activity 2.3: sketch a hydrogen atom
steps: Draw a small circle and label it "nucleus".
Inside it draw a smaller circle and label it "proton" (+).
Draw a bigger circle around the nucleus: the electron shell.
Put one dot on it and label it "electron" (−).
Common hydrogen has no neutron, so do not draw one.

screens.text: Parts of the atom: which particles are in the nucleus?
screens.why:
The nucleus is the tiny centre of the atom.
It holds the protons and the neutrons.
The electrons move outside it, in shells.
So the answer is protons and neutrons.
screens.clue: Which one moves around the outside?

screens.text: Subatomic particles: match each particle with its relative charge.
screens.why:
Proton: positive, +1.
Electron: negative, −1.
Neutron: neutral, 0. (Neutron sounds like neutral.)

screens.text: Mass of particles, true or false: a proton and an electron have about the same mass.
screens.why:
Proton: 1.673 × 10⁻²⁴ g.
Electron: 9.109 × 10⁻²⁸ g, about 1800–2000 times lighter.
It is the proton and the NEUTRON that have about the same mass.
So the statement is false.

screens.title: Proton, neutron or electron?
screens.text: Subatomic particles: sort each clue to the particle it describes.
items: About 1800–2000 times lighter than a proton.
Its number is the atomic number
screens.why:
Proton: charge +1, in the nucleus; the atomic number counts protons.
Neutron: no charge, in the nucleus.
Electron: charge −1, outside the nucleus, almost no mass.
screens.clue: Think of each particle's charge and where it is.

screens.text: Charge of an atom: why is an atom electrically neutral?
opts: It has equal numbers of protons and electrons
screens.ans: It has equal numbers of protons and electrons
screens.why:
Each proton has a charge of +1.
Each electron has a charge of −1.
An atom has the same number of each.
So the charges cancel: total charge 0.
Neutrons have no charge, so they do not change this.

screens.text: The nucleus: which statement about it is correct?
opts: It fills most of the atom's volume
screens.why:
The nucleus holds protons (+1) and neutrons (0).
There are no negative particles inside it.
So its charge is always positive.
It is tiny: the electrons take up most of the volume.

screens.text: Size of an atom: if a nucleus were the size of a football in the middle of Addis Ababa Stadium, where would the electrons be?
opts: Far away, around the outer seats
screens.ans: Far away, around the outer seats
screens.why:
The nucleus is tiny compared with the whole atom.
The electrons move far out, in shells around it.
Most of the atom's volume is taken up by the electrons.
So they would be far away, around the outer seats.
An atom is mostly empty space.
screens.clue: Which part takes up most of the volume?

en.text: The atomic number Z is the number of protons; in a neutral atom it also equals the number of electrons. The mass number A is protons + neutrons. So neutrons = A − Z. In the notation ¹²₆C, 12 is the mass number and 6 the atomic number.

am.text: አቶሚክ ቁጥር (Z) የፕሮቶኖች ቁጥር ነው፤ በገለልተኛ አቶም የኤሌክትሮኖችም ቁጥር ነው። የክብደት ቁጥር (A) ፕሮቶን + ኒውትሮን ነው። ኒውትሮን = A − Z።

screens.title: Read the label
screens.ask: A carbon atom is written ¹²₆C. How many protons does it have?
screens.after: 6. The bottom number is the atomic number, which counts the protons.

screens.title: Atomic number and mass number
paras: The atomic number (Z) equals the number of protons in the nucleus.
In a neutral atom it is also the number of electrons.
The mass number (A) is the number of protons plus the number of neutrons.

screens.title: The notation
paras: We write an atom as ᴬ_Z X.
A (top left) is the mass number, Z (bottom left) is the atomic number, X is the symbol.
¹²₆C: mass number 12, atomic number 6, symbol C for carbon.

screens.title: Read the label ¹²₆C
screens.ask: Tap each part of the label.
items: Atomic number Z: 6 protons. The neutral atom also has 6 electrons.
The symbol of the element: carbon.

screens.title: Build a nucleus
outs: Electrons in the neutral atom = Z
screens.note: 6 protons and 6 neutrons give ¹²₆C. Try 7 and 7 for nitrogen, ¹⁴₇N. Adding a neutron changes A, but not Z.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The number of protons in the nucleus, written Z. In a neutral atom it also equals the number of electrons.
The number of protons plus the number of neutrons, written A.

screens.title: ¹⁴₇N: protons, electrons, neutrons
steps: Electrons = Z = 7, because the atom is neutral.

screens.ask: Neutrons from the notation: ²⁴₁₂Mg has ___ neutrons
screens.why:
Top number: mass number A = 24.
Bottom number: atomic number Z = 12.
Neutrons = A − Z.
24 − 12 = 12 neutrons.
screens.clue: Subtract the bottom number from the top number.

screens.text: Key words: the sum of the numbers of protons and neutrons is the
screens.why:
Protons and neutrons are both in the nucleus.
Their total is the mass number, A.
The atomic number, Z, counts only the protons.
So the answer is mass number.
screens.clue: Which number counts everything in the nucleus?

screens.ask: Mass number: a nucleus has 9 protons and 10 neutrons. Its mass number = ___
screens.why:
Mass number = protons + neutrons.
9 + 10 = 19.
So A = 19.

screens.text: Atomic number: that atom has 9 protons. Which element is it?
screens.why:
The number of protons is the atomic number: Z = 9.
Each element has its own atomic number.
In the periodic table, Z = 9 is fluorine (F).
Oxygen is 8 and neon is 10.
screens.clue: The atomic number tells the element.

screens.ask: Electrons from the notation: ¹⁶₈O has ___ electrons
screens.why:
Bottom number: Z = 8, so 8 protons.
A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons.
So it has 8 electrons.
The top number, 16, is not the electron count.
screens.clue: In a neutral atom, electrons = protons.

screens.text: Atomic number, true or false: different elements have the same number of protons.
screens.why:
The number of protons is the atomic number.
It tells you which element an atom is.
Carbon has 6, nitrogen 7, oxygen 8.
So different elements have different numbers. False.
screens.clue: What makes carbon different from oxygen?

screens.ask: Mass number: an atom has 11 electrons and 12 neutrons. Its mass number = ___
screens.why:
A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons.
So protons = 11.
Mass number = protons + neutrons = 11 + 12 = 23.
This atom is sodium (Na), Z = 11.
screens.clue: First find the protons from the electrons.

items.ask: Activity 2.5, neutrons: lithium has Z = 3 and A = 7. Neutrons = ___
items.why:
Neutrons = A − Z.
7 − 3 = 4.
So lithium has 4 neutrons.

items.ask: Activity 2.5, neutrons: neon has Z = 10 and A = 20. Neutrons = ___
items.why:
Neutrons = A − Z.
20 − 10 = 10.
So neon has 10 neutrons.

items.ask: Activity 2.5, electrons: helium has Z = 2. Electrons = ___
items.why:
Z = 2, so helium has 2 protons.
A neutral atom has equal protons and electrons.
So helium has 2 electrons.

items.text: Exercise 2.2, parts of the atom: match each particle with where it is found.

Protons are in the nucleus.

Electrons are outside the nucleus, in shells.

items.why:

So A = 19.

test.text: Subatomic particles: the electron has a relative charge of
test.why:
Electrons are negative particles.
Their relative charge is −1.
Protons are +1 and neutrons are 0.

test.text: Key words: atomic number is the number of
test.why:
The atomic number, Z, counts the protons in the nucleus.
Protons + neutrons is the mass number, A.
So the answer is protons.

Mass number: an atom has 17 protons and 18 neutrons. Mass number = ___
test.why:
Mass number = protons + neutrons.
17 + 18 = 35.
So A = 35 (this atom is chlorine).

test.text: Atomic number: an atom has 20 electrons. Its atomic number is
test.why:
A neutral atom has equal protons and electrons.
So it has 20 protons.
The atomic number counts protons: Z = 20.
40 would be a mass number, not an atomic number.
